name: Blockwise-Addressing
definition: Following Example 2 of \cite{ben1997online}, fix $d\ge2$ with $d\mid 2^d$ and put $m=2^d$.  The domain is $\{z,x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_m\}$.  There are $2m$ concepts $f_1,\ldots,f_m,g_1,\ldots,g_m$.  Each $f_i$ has $f_i(z)=0$, is the $i$th singleton on the $x$-coordinates, and, on each of $m/d$ blocks of $d$ $y$-coordinates, the words $(f_i)$ run through all $2^d$ binary patterns (the same indexing in every block).  Symmetrically, $g_i(z)=1$, is the $i$th singleton on the $y$-coordinates, and its values on each $x$-block run through all $d$-bit patterns.  The source proves $M_{sd}\le2$ and $M_{best}=\Omega(d)=\Omega(\log |\mathcal X|)$.  The direct teaching argument recorded in the value entries gives $RTD=2$.
